text_fidelity_a:
ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large We have company coming this summer. This involves a few tents, but one of the people needs an inflatable mattress and room for stuff. This tent is who we got this for.

ASSEMBLY
Assembly was not difficult in our trial run. The instructions were pretty easy to follow and it does not take more than a half hour to put up with two people unless you are with someone VERY efficient in putting up tents.

WITHOUT FLY
Without the fly, this is a very nice tent - bright, airy, and lots of upper mesh to see the sky. This is perfect on nice days.

WITH FLY
The days that rain might be expected are the challenge. The fly is dark blue. The dark blue makes this tent feel very warm and almost oppressive some days, but it does protect in the rain. My point is if you are the type who does not want to take the fly off and put it on constantly, this might be a big dark for you to leave on constantly, unless you plan to just sleep inside and don't care.

STAKES
The stakes that come with this are not big enough to support the weight of wind and other frustrations. We got spiral stakes to use with this at least on the key points of stress and it works better.

STURDY?
We are only using this for this summer, so hopefully it will last through several weeks of use. We have not had any high winds or severe storms yet so I will have to update as to how well this worked for that.

STORM PROOFING
One thing we learned about tents over long term is that double tarps are a good idea. We put one down under the tent leaving a perimeter that is not too big around the edge. Then we put another inside the tent to further protect should there be a deluge.

STORAGE
I find that having a separate nylon bag for the fly helps a lot when it comes time to put this tent away. It allows for a faster pick up time and less frustrating trying to make everything fit.

SIZE
This is perfect for a queen sized mattress, 1 or 2 people and their stuff.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is great for a family with sleeping bags and not much stuff, or for less people and more stuff. The stakes could be better, the storage bag bigger, and perhaps a bit tougher construction/fabric, but all in all this is a decent tent and serves our purpose well- I hope.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS at this point. I will update once summer is over as to the longevity of this tent over several weeks.
text_fidelity_b: ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large

Fire Blanket for Home Kitchen Safety – Fiberglass Blankets Suspend Fire Flames Suspension Prepared for Kitchen School Fireplace Grill Car Garage House Warehouse Camp RV Safety Hero (2, 3.3ft x 3.3ft) Cooking on open flame in my kitchen makes me worried that grease or something nearby catching fire, so I was delighted to find these fire blankets!

I've seen similar ones in the kitchen at the hotel my daughter manages, but I didn't know they were also available for homes.

These are just the right size for my 36" gas cooktop, and obviously they would work as well for a smaller size cooktop, for most grills, fire pits, or to smother flames on a small child's clothing.

Made of woven glass fibers, each blanket comes in a durable Velcro closing bag with a heavy duty grommet for hanging.

You can hang them discretely in a cabinet near your cooktop, on a garage wall, near your BBQ grill, or even take one along when camping. The main thing is to place them near enough to the potential fire area to reach quickly.

Should you need to smother a fire, pull down on the Velcro tabs and the blanket will come out easily.

Shake to unfold it then cover the front of your body as you approach the flames, lay the blanket over the flames and then back away until the fire is completely extinguished.

Once the fire is put out and things have cooled down you can remove the blanket, fold it back up and tuck it back into its container to use again if needed.

Be sure to wear protective gloves when folding and placing the blanket back in its container though, because your hands will get lots of fiberglass shards in them otherwise and having just made that mistake I speak from experience when I tell you that hurts!

I'm so happy to have several of these in the house now though. One for the kitchen and the other's going out by the grill.

No more worry about fire extinguishers that might be out of date or not work. A game changer!
text_fidelity_b: Fire Blanket for Home Kitchen Safety – Fiberglass Blankets Suspend Fire Flames Suspension Prepared for Kitchen School Fireplace Grill Car Garage House Warehouse Camp RV Safety Hero (2, 3.3ft x 3.3ft)

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Aspect DSLR Large Shoulder Bag, Black I have a really nice 12 year old Olympus camera that has been all over the world with me and has documented my best memories & experiences. The different carrying cases have never lived up to the expectations or sometimes harsh environments my beloved camera has.

This Thule bag is surprisingly well made and much bigger than my best case. (See the photo for side by side comparison) This bag holds my camera and a portable tripod with some finagling of the included padded pieces. Those pieces are designed with Velcro to fit and attach in whatever shape or spot you need - which means you aren't limited to using only items that fit in pre-made pockets.

The zippered lid pocket has a perfect pouch for batteries, USB cords and other small odds and ends. Inside the bag is a separate pocket for a tablet. Once I put my camera and tripod in, my 10" Fire will only fit if I take the case off of it first, so that's not great. There are two elastic pockets on the outside and a flat front zippered pocket on the front with a snap for your keys. Conceivably, you could hit the trail with just this bag carrying your camera stuff, a bottle of water, your id & keys and maybe a light, small snack. I have had this out at the barn & a horse show for photos of the horses and it works fine, but it will take some time to get used to the bulk of this bag for trekking through a jungle or climbing ruins in Central America or Asia.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Aspect DSLR Large Shoulder Bag, Black

Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds) I've been hunting with Mathews compound bows for 20 years and reached a point in my age that I wanted to switch to a crossbow. I wanted to find the best bow for the money to start out. I like compounds but I wanted to stay as basic and simple as I could with the crossbow for service and maintaining accuracy so I wanted a recurve.
Long story short the Excaliburs are nice but to rich for my blood so I took a chance on the Wildfire II based on the reviews. I'm glad that I did.
Pros:
Excellent fit and finsh work on the entire bow. Definitely quality construction on par with any of the big name crossbow makers.
It seems as fast and they say it is. Once sighted in it is consistently accurate. I think this bow is on par with the Excalibur baseline bows Like the Axiom or Ibex if not better as this bow has a one peice Aluminum rail versus a plastic rail. Weight is not bad at all and it feels well balanced for free hand shooting. Soft touch Camo is awesome and a nice balance of pattern and color.
Thumb Safety just like a rifle. Not up on the side of the string latch like a lot of other crossbows and quiet as a mouse. Not a loud CLICK! when you take the safety off. The trigger does have some creep but is pretty smooth overall. The more I shoot the better it gets.
Shot noise is average and less than a pellet gun for comparison. It comes with factory installed limb dampeners that attach to the riser/limb. I also installed the SIMS LIMBSAVER kit and it definitely helped reduce the sound when fired.
Scope is actually very good quality and clarity. Super clean reticle and the adjustable illumination is great for early morning/late evening shots! I was thinking to buy a Nikon but this scope is really nice so I will keep using it.
Rope cocker, Arrows, quiver, and sling are very nice quality as well. Super sling swivels too!
Must haves:
Plano Soft bow case. Best priced case that actually fits the bow another really good option is the OMP Crossbow soft case. A little more in cost but has additional pockets for arrows etc.
Tenpoint ACUrope cocker (BEST). Compact and retractable. Works like a dream and has a belt pouch.
Carbon Express Bolts. Either the Piledrivers or if you want the best get the Maxima Hunters. Buy their lighted nocks for your hunting arrows.
Go ahead and buy the MTM bolt case for your extra bolts.
Scorpion Venom string wax. The bow comes with string wax but I feel the Scorpion is easier to use and stays super slick in all weather.
Rail lube. DO NOT USE STRING WAX! I did and it slowed down the bow and killed my accuracy. I had to clean the rail with rubbing alcohol and start over. Buy Excalibur rail lube and/or do some research on the bow forums on what the veteran shooters are using. Some recommend silicone spray and other types of lube. If you're going to hunt use something that doesn't have any odor. I ended up using Ultralube 4x. It's all natural and no odor.
NAP 100 grain Sptifire Edge mechanical broadheads. These are my personal favorite and for overall accuracy I prefer mechanicals over fixed blades for better flight at high speeds.
Target for field point is the Hurricane H25 hands down best practice target for the money. It stops the bolts no matter what and is heavy and stable. You don't need a stand for it.
Target for broadheads I recommend the Blobtarget or American white tale HybriMAT AP . They are both pricey (BT 18"x18"x10" $90 shppied) (HybriMAT AP 18"x18"x12" $129.95 shipped) but they will last you for years and years vs the cheaper ones that last a year and are still very expensive!
Update:
Bought a Prochrono on Amazon to check the speed of the bow and right now it is 315fps with the stock arrows and with the Maxima Hunters. Dyna Flight string should bring it up to as much as 330fps.
I ended up removing the limbsavers since they slowed it down (10fps!) and actually created vibration in the bow after the shot. To be honest the noise level is not much different without them.
Another update. Bow is shooting 330fps using Carbon Express 20" hunter maximas and 100gr tips. I switched to Black Eagle Spynal Tapp arrows and the speed is still on.
Final deer season tally is 3 does and i buck
text_fidelity_b: Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds)

SOG Tactical Tomahawk- Throwing Hatchet, Versatile Survival Tactical Axe and Emergency Breaching Tool with Sheath (F01TN-CP) In Vietnam, American Special Forces soldiers soon learned a lesson their ancestors knew very well--a tomahawk is better than a knife for close combat. In spite of its popularity, my own opinion of the Vietnam tomahawk has always been that it's a wimpy little ax, with a head that's too small for real work and a handle that will snap like a twig. It's a crude blunt instrument that looks like an ax. The SOG Fusion Tactical Tomahawk takes the concept behind the Vietnam Special Forces ax and gets rid of the many problems.

Weight is a major concern whether you are a hunter or a soldier, and you need a lot of positives to carry a 24 oz axe as a regular part of your kit. The SOG Fusion justifies every ounce. The steel ax head, with the traditional military spike for balance, has a 2 3/4" straight edge that's properly ground so you can efficiently chop wood or heavy bone. Hunters of big game often find a small ax to be more efficient at butchering tasks than a heavy knife, something nearly everyone knew in the frontier days.

The weakest point of the old Vietnam axe was the wooden handle, too thin at the juncture with the axe head to be reliable. The Fusion has a much less destructible fiberglass handle with rubberized grip. Once marketed as "unbreakable," fiberglass proved to be much less than perfect as a tool handle. The tang and rivet attachment of head to handle that you see in the Fusion is an excellent solution to the old issue of head separation, a puzzle that smiths have battled for centuries. Used with some skill, this combination really should last forever. In camp you'll find it's endlessly practical.

Medium fits 55-58CM (22.2"-22.8");
Large fits 58-61CM (23.03"- 24.0") ----my head measures 23.75", this fits very well.

Despite that the product description states that the hat is adjustable, it is NOT. The only portion that is "adjustable" is the optional chin strap. On mine, it can be kept clipped on, or taken off. There is a toggle to make it tighter against the face, or allow it to be loose.

The interior has what appears to be an elastic band, but it is not elastic. It's purpose is more like that of a sweat band or to provide some grip, but it doesn't not stretch. This will either fit, or it won't.

I normally like Jeff & Aimmy products, and overall I like this too. I just want to see a cleaned up, more accurate description. (and what are with all the reviews for this product yet are for something not being sold here?)

The material is soft, light. The brim is long but can be folded back some as needed.
The slit for the pony tail is subtle. So it will blend in when not in use. But to use it, is a little awkward as you will have to feed the pony tail through a narrow slit. Not bad though. Doable.

I do appreciate that there are size offerings for larger heads. It is rare- extremely- that I find a womens hat that fits anything above 22.5". MY cranium is 23.75", so I can't wear most stuff. SO unless you have a bigger head like mine, you will most likely be wanting a medium. If your "large" is too big, then you ordered the wrong size as the size large is accurate (23.03"- 24.0"). It will just fit if your head it 24". Might be snug. It fits mine just right at 23.75". Or if your medium is too small.. then again, likely wrong size. selected. Either way, make sure you got what you ordered.

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple) Your first observation might be similar to mine. The outdoor setting is calming and just gorgeous. The colors in this video are beautiful and the river creates a calm, quiet and peaceful setting for your workout.

I enjoyed the workout, but didn't realize how many muscles you needed to perch yourself atop a balance ball. You start off just rolling over the ball and then progress to some pretty tough balancing acts. There are some stretches which will stretch out your spine in new ways. I realized I'm not as flexible as I thought I was.

I'd advise watching this video at least once before proceeding because it is kinda difficult to follow the workout while attempting to focus on not hurtling towards the floor if you are not totally focused on what you are doing.

The kit includes:

Medium inflatable exercise ball (green, 26"/65cm)
Full-length workout video (35 minutes)
Air pump

The Air pump is "ok," but I found that an electric pump was much more efficient. If you use the air pump, you might want to do that "workout" the day before. The instruction scare you into worrying about inflating the ball too much, but never fear, with that pump, it might be impossible.

The medium exercise ball is "ok" but had I realized there was a larger balance ball, I'd have ordered the larger one since I'm taller. If you are 5' 9" and above, I'd say go for the blue balance ball (large size). I think weight also counts. If you are above your recommended weight (ideal weight and all that), then you might want a larger size.

On the side of the box it says:

Small Purple Balance Ball - Height 5' 0" to 5' 5" - Ball Size 22"/55cm
Medium Green Balance Ball - Height 5' 6 to 5' 11" - Ball Size 26"/65cm
Large Blue Balance Ball - Height 6' 0" to 6' 3" - Ball Size 30"/75cm

The exercise video is combination of shorter segments from three balance ball workouts. You really have to concentrate on making smooth and steady movements.

The way I found this workout to be most effective was to place the ball on top of a yoga mat. This prevents slippage of the ball on a carpet and also prevents you from getting injured because the yoga mat provides an additional level of protection from your hands and feet slipping on a carpet.

You will be doing three workouts.

Upper Body
Abs
Lower Body

There are times when you are either sitting, leaning over the ball or on your back, balancing and stretching out your spine. The hardest part of this workout is when you are on you back and you are rolling on top the ball. It is easier once you make full use of your powers of concentration.

The video is a nice introduction, but is really only an introduction. While you can get a good beginner's workout, I'd imagine it is more effective to order the three additional videos they recommend. Karen Voight also has a DVD out called BLT (Butt, Legs & Tummy) on a ball.

This workout will take you to new levels of concentration and mind-body awareness. It will work the upper body, lower body and abs. You will be strengthening, toning and conditioning smaller core muscles.

The 45 minutes includes a 5-minute warm-up to learn proper positioning.

If you enjoy this workout, look for:

BalanceBall Fitness Upper Body Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Abs Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Lower Body Workout

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
G4Free Sport Outdoor Waist Pack Tactical Sling Bag Hiking Fanny Pack Fishing Tackles What a GREAT pack! When I agreed to write an honest review in return for a tan pack, I was thinking this would be a slight improvement over your run-of-the-mill fanny packs. OMG, this thing is brilliantly designed! It's got so many nooks and crannies and mesh pockets and loops and cinches and straps, all very thoughtfully laid out, that it makes you want to go somewhere just so you can load it up and wear it. It would be a great pack for an emergency bug-out bag. Now I know what I'll keep my emergency mylar blankets, waterproof matches, and dynamo flashlight in so if we have another bad winter like this past year they'll be totally handy.

The way this pack is designed, I can see myself using it as my only purse and keeping the major essentials in it at all times. The included shoulder strap would make this very doable, but I like it that the strap can be removed if you want to carry it by the top handle and/ or wear it as a fanny pack. The Big Costco Buy would definitely be easier if I wore this at my waist instead of trying to carrying a purse. The way it's designed, the zippers in the top compartment, which is the logical place to put money and credit cards and a cell phone, face toward your body when you are wearing this as a fanny pack, which adds a level of security whether you're in a store or on the trail. It is so flexible in terms of what you can do with it that I'm just knocked out. I really do love it!

The largest compartment is not quite wide enough for my ASUS MeMO Pad FHD 10 (10.1") tablet, not if I want to zip it around all the way, but it holds my Kindle Paperwhite in a Versa leather-look case and only misses being able to hold the tablet by a bit. It may be that when the stiffness of the fabric and zippers loosens up with use, as it will, the tablet will fit fine and the zipper will close all the way.

This pack looks pretty indestructible, too, for a fabric pack. It is very well sewn and fortified, and if I had not been given this pack for review, if I had seen one up close and personal when kicking around town, I would have wanted one and asked where the person got it. Don't even hesitate.

text_fidelity_a: Soft SnooZ'zzz® Deluxe - Get a Deep, Relaxing, Light-Free Sleep. Anytime, Anywhere. Unisex Eye Mask. Protective Carry Pouch Included with Sleeping Mask. I am no stranger to sleep masks. I am always searching for one that is better than the one I am using. I saw this one and decided to purchase it.  I will say that I disagree with the description calling it a "larger" size sleep mask. It definitely is not that.  When I got the package in the mail, I opened the mask and thought this is way too small for me. BUT, I soon realized that while average in size, this sleep mask is really amazing!  First, it isn't the typical fabric (satin) that you find in masks.  It is a sort of microfiber fabric. It really helps the mask stay in place while sleeping. It isn't fancy as far as the way you put it on. It is the same velcro you find in nearly all masks. I remedy this by sewing a tube of fabric around the velcro part because I don't like it pulling my hair.  I was amazed at how well this small mask really does block out the light.  I am almost ready to say that it blocks out light better than any of the dozens of masks I have purchased over the years.  All in all, I am super happy with my purchased and I would recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Soft SnooZ'zzz® Deluxe - Get a Deep, Relaxing, Light-Free Sleep. Anytime, Anywhere. Unisex Eye Mask. Protective Carry Pouch Included with Sleeping Mask.

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

text_fidelity_a:
MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking UPADATED AGAIN: I have purchased both the 1 and 2 person tent. Seems like very well quality and lightweight. However, the ONE thing that is bad about BOTH tents is the way the end tie outs are sewn and sealed. The tents BOTH leak at the tie out points. This is due to the way they are sealed. It seams as if the seam seal was applied FIRST and then the tie outs sewn into the fabric. This allows water to come through the stitching and leak into the tent. POOR DESIGN. I have remedied this by using seam sealant on ALL stitch points for the tie outs. So, word of caution for everyone owning and buying these tents. MAKE SURE YOU SEAM SEAL EVERY TIE OUT POINT. Once you do that, this tent should be waterproof.

UPDATE: I set this tent up in my yard to test it for waterproof and durability. We had a rain event that came through. No heavy storms. Just light to medium rain that only lasted 10 or 15 minutes. The tent leaked at both ends where the tie outs are sewn into the fabric. These points are seam sealed, so I do not know why or how it leaked at both points. The water on the floor of the tent was about the size of a quarter.
I have since sprayed all of the fly seams and the tie out points with silicone treatment. When we get another rain storm coming through, I will set it up again for another test to see if the spray will keep the tie out points from leaking.
Also, both sides and the rear of the fly, down at the edge, collect water and allow it to pool up. This is a design flaw. I had the tent as tight as I could get it, without damaging the material. The water pooled up around the bottom edge looked like a small moat, and could lead to large amounts of water to run under the tent. This could soak through the floor and get your sleeping gear wet.
I fixed this issue with some micro tarp clamps and 550 cord. I attached one at each end, and two in the rear, one on each side between the rear stake out point and each corner. So 4 total. When I set the tent up again for another rain test, I will update with pictures.
So far, this tent was NOT the tent that all the hype was about. The ONLY positive thing so far, is that it is a true double wall tent, and that will keep condensation out of the sleeping area.

I have not used this tent yet, only set it up. However, with just having set it up, I can see that I will probably like this tent. But, one thing I would like to have seen with it, is more fabric at the vestibule. When set up by the directions, the edge of the vestibule is quite high off of the ground. This would allow for good ventilation during a summer night, but in a rain storm, I would be afraid of rain being blown in.
I have it set up in the yard, and we have a chance of rain today/tonight, so once I let it get rained on and take it out on a trip, I will update my review.
text_fidelity_b: MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins with Mesh Bag, Yellow, Large/X-Large I really wanted to like these black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG with the adjustable heal strap and open heel. I needed a size 11 short fin for long distance endurance swimming in a harness in my pool year-round. I did not need a fin that was too buoyant and would make me lazy in my kicking.

I compared the yellow and black Phantom Aquatics Speed Sport Adjustable Snorkeling Fins L/XL (size 9-13); the US Swim Divers Grey and Black Large Fitness Fins; the black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG; the SEAC Black (Large 9.5 --11) Fins with the fixed heal strap and open heel; and the TYR BP Burner Fins LG (size 11 -- Blue & Black).

First off I had to send back the large SEAC's and large TYR EP Burner's to get the XL size in each. Both of them were painfully tight on my size 11 feet.

The worst first. The yellow and black Phantom Aquatics Speed Sport Adjustable Snorkeling Fins L/XL (size 9-13) are for snorkeling and not for training of any kind. The boot and heel strap are amazingly comfortable and strong, but the composite fin is too long and whippy for training in either a pool or open water. I would not even want to do kick sets with these. I personally would not even want to use these for snorkeling because I would always be waiting for the tips of my fins to catch up to what I was trying to do in the water to position myself for snorkeling/sightseeing.

The disappointment next. The U.S. Swim Divers Large Fitness Fins had an open heel which I generally prefer because I wear different booties during the 12 months of the year. The length of the boot was perfect, the heel strap was strong, easily adjusted, and comfortable, and the boots felt really comfortable in shape and foot support EXCEPT for the constant pressure on the knuckle of the little toe on each foot. I'm absolutely a typical size 11, but they hurt my foot, and if you have a slightly thicker or wider size 10.5--11 foot go up to the XL. I personally didn't order the next size up because while I was kicking with them I could really feel that this fin was not stiff enough for training, and certainly not for kick sets. The rubber fin was bending too easily on every kick at the seam just beyond my toes on both fins - IMOP a serious design flaw for a "fitness fin." I could never do kick sets in these, but I could use these for snorkeling since the tips of the fins do spring back almost quickly enough to be responsive to my changes in direction and speed.

SO COMFORTABLE BUT SO LONG. The black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG had a great shaped boot, a strong, easily adjusted, and flexible heel strap, and they were absolutely the MOST comfortable boot of all those I tried, BUT these were definitely a better snorkeling fin and/or an open-water training fin. They were absolutely strong enough for open water training (which I rarely get to do anymore), but too way too long for endurance training in a pool with a harness. If these were 2 inches shorter they would have been my overall pick of a stiff training fin.

I liked the way the SEAC Black Fins looked, but had to go up to the X-Large (11-12.5) and they were perfect. They have the fixed heal strap which I usually don't prefer, but this one is strong and stretchy enough to be very comfortable. The open heel did not make my feet feel unsupported at all. With barefeet they were a little soft, but with a 2mm or 5mm neoprene bootie they fit my feet perfectly. The front of the boot is comfortable lengthwise and widthwise, and there's no unnecessary gimmics in the fin design. As the ad says these are ideal for open water snorkeling for a good swimmer, and ideal for pool training. The fin is short enough and stiff enough for what I wanted to do. I can do flutter kicks or slow subtle kicks just to keep my feet afloat when I am working on my upper body. The fins do not add any extra buoyancy which I don't need with easy kicking or with a wetsuit on six months of the year. I am so glad I loved these.

I just had to try something new with the TYR BP Burner Fins LG (size 11 -- Red & Black). They had to be exchanged for the XL - the Blue and Black, and I feared they might be too big, but I found they have a very stretchy and supportive heel pocket, that was as comfortable and supportive as the adjustable heel straps I usually prefer. The TYR EP Burners boot will be my spring and summer fins as they fit my naked foot or with a 2mm bootie perfectly. It's good that the fin is just that short because just another inch or so and the fin would be too flexible. Perfect design by TYR for a training fin. As the ad says "The perfect fins for training at race cadence." I kept these for warmer water training and the SEAC's for cold water training. I would use each of these for snorkeling, as I am a strong swimmer and I want my fins to be very responsive to the demand I am putting on them to change direction or to accelerate and change speed.

I was not asked to give this review or compensated by anyone. Happy training.
text_fidelity_b: Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins with Mesh Bag, Yellow, Large/X-Large

text_fidelity_a:
Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person Update: We returned the original tent and dually had a chance to use the replacement sent and......

Same exact problem. Almost no wind, light rain and the poles bent at a ridiculous angle before snapping. Wenzel is the worst brand of tent I've ever used. Can't return it since it was last season's replacement so we sound up throwing what was left away. I regret not Judy buying a Coleman for the same price when I had the chance.
I'll start out saying that Wenzel in general is a very quality name and usually makes quality products. That being said I was very unhappy with this particular tent. Despite the usual common sense I have when I buy gear I didn't check the package before heading out (entirely my fault there). It's a good thing I keep a just in case kit in our vehicle because there were no pegs at all in the package, not even the little peg bag (and yes, It was bought new and still in the package as well as the Amazon box). No big deal there, just a minor annoyance.

I set the tent up with help of another avid camper friend of mine who's had this same exact tent for about a year and uses it like crazy. About two hours later a small sprinkling rain came up with some soft wind. His kids were enjoying tent time and listening to the rain when suddenly one of the poles splintered very quickly and sliced open my arm a few inches. suffice to say it was a very bad day and there were a several spooked and unhappy children as their dad had to take us all through the backwoods to a clinic so I could get stitches. Not the best birthday party a kid can have. I have had a couple of tents splinter their poles before but it's never been so violent nor had such a brittle quality to it. They've looked more like shreds while this just broke off in several jagged pieces and a few very sharp splinters left behind.

This is not the usual Wenzel quality and I'm hoping it's just a fluke. Perhaps it's the design? A badly handled or worn out pole? I don't know. But be aware that this might be a problem. Going through one of the many reviews I did find one where a woman had a pole splinter suddenly and go in to her hand. I wish I'd found that review before buying. I'm returning this one to Amazon for replacement in hopes that it was just one of those random things and will update if it happens again.
text_fidelity_b: Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person

Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) The device works fine. I really like the e-mail and text alerts.

What I don't like: THE BAND. I purchased this device in December 2016 and didn't get around to wearing it until January 2017. It is now March. The band has broken TWICE -- it comes detached on the buckle side, where the band attaches to the device. Once it becomes detached, it will never stay secure again. Although I can slide it back together, it easily comes off when I'm pulling off a coat or a sweater. I can understand this happening once, but TWICE??? Never had this problem with my Charge.

Fortunately, FITBIT customer service is very helpful. They have sent replacement bands at no charge, which I truly appreciate. However, I would much prefer the device just stayed in one piece and I didn't have to mess with the replacement band over and over. I've tried to figure out if I'm doing something wrong -- but the instructions for replacing the bands are pretty straight-forward, so I'm not sure how you'd go wrong.

Overall, I like the functionality of the device but sure wish the band would stop breaking!

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

First I transported a huge load of dirty linen for my wife from her massage therapy business to the laundry via scooter (3/4 capacity). Then I swung by Trader Joe's supermarket and loaded up at least 30 lbs of food and scootered home (2/5 capacity).

The Mier backpack performed extremely well. The 60L volume is HUGE. Huuuge. I am 6' tall, 215 lbs, fit. This is ALL you need for standard transport. The 150L (at more than double the volume of the 60L) should be able to hold a body... A use for the 150L would likely be transporting bulky, light loads (e.g., 25 food trays that need to be kept vertical).

These are truly MEGA packs.

Padding on the straps is decent for usage in 30 minute stints under max load or all day under light loads. The only downside was my back sopping with sweat due to the pack exterior not being made of breathable material.

Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Solio Xcellerator and HUB Battery Pack, Black/White Bit biased Solio "fanboy". Second Solio product purchased. Bolt user for 3 seasons of heavy use in some relatively extreme conditions. Only issue with the Bolt has been the expected loss of battery capacity due to use. Solio has provided a replacement battery free of charge. Reliable product with over the top customer service.

Charged up the hub using a wall plug. Have been sitting here on the deck under a partly cloudy sky with the panel plugged into the Hub, the Hub plugged into the iPad Mini Retina. Over the past hour the iPad battery has gone from 68 to 69%. The Hub capacity has dropped from 100 to 60-80%. iPad Mini Retina battery capacity is +6000mAh. Hub capacity is 2000mAh. On paper the maximum topping off charge should be ~33%. Under current levels of sunlight the panel as expected cannot maintain full Hub charge.

Conclusion:
Option for Apple specific charging protocol and minimal risk if you charge via the Hub to your device are big positives. The big negative is not specific to this charger. The neg. are the limits of today's solar panels.
This is a small, relatively light in weight and compact solar panel. The rate it charges the Hub has to be balanced against the panel size. If you can deal with the charging rate and are in need of a compact, lighter weight unit you will probably like this
product. Limited capacity of the Hub battery are IMO a negative. The Classic2 has a 3700mAh battery. Would be happier if
Solio could increase the capacity of the Hub. Test of time and higher capacity battery for today's higher energy needs limits this solar charger to 4****s for now.
text_fidelity_b: Solio Xcellerator and HUB Battery Pack, Black/White

text_fidelity_a:
Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch These stakes are well-constructed and can be pounded into reasonably hard soil without damage. I haven't destroyed any yet, but I do try to be careful when I'm pounding them into rocky ground. (A small, 8-ounce hammer works well. Larger hammers increase the likelihood of bending or breaking your stakes). The round cross section doesn't have the holding power of some of the flatter stake designs, so they don't hold as well in wind, in my experience. They're longer than most other after-market tent stakes, though (9 inches vs the more common 7-inches), which helps compensate. I like to have a few of these in my stake bag for places that the y-shaped stakes can't penetrate.

Some users have complained that they can't get their tent guylines through the holes in the silver heads. That isn't how they are intended to be used. Wrap your guyline or your anchor loop around the shaft of the stake, just below the silver head, and angle your stake to point it toward a point several feet below the center of your tent. These are fine stakes. Would like to try some of this style in a longer, 12-inch version, for larger tents that catch more wind and require stronger anchors.
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch

text_fidelity_a: Gootus Bike Wall Mount - Horizontal Bike Wall Rack Hanger for Garage or Home | Heavy Duty Bicycle Wall Mounted Holder for Road, Mountain or Hybrid Bikes Much more compact storage than hanging perpendicular to the wall by a wheel. Bike hangs at about a 15 degree angle off the wall by one of the pedals on the goofy-looking, but very strong hanger bracket. The tires are supported by two L-shaped brackets on the wall. If you are mounting on a standard stud/sheetrock wall, BE SURE TO SCREW THE HANGER BRACKET INTO A WALL STUD. The hanger bracket does the work of supporting the bike and molly bolts or sheetrock anchors will not be strong enough. The manufacturer recommends installing only on a masonry wall, but if you attach to a wall stud, it will be fine. You can use sheetrock anchors for the tire brackets, since they don't really hold the weight of the bike, they more keep the bike aligned and stable. Very easy to get the bike on and off.

Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.
